name: Cayman Islands
summary: The Cayman Islands have no forced heirship. Cayman trusts are protected by statute against foreign forced-heirship claims and a foundation company (2017) is available. The Hague Trusts Convention is not listed as extended to Cayman.
foreign_law_note: Immovable property in Cayman is governed by Cayman law; movable property follows the law of the deceased's domicile (Ogier, via search summary). There is no choice of nationality law.
trust_note: Cayman is not on the UK's HCCH extension list. Trusts Act (2021 Revision): courts will not recognise forced-heirship claims against a Cayman trust (foreign-element provisions, since 1987); s. 90 governing law. STAR trusts allow purpose trusts. Foundation Companies Act (2017) applies Trusts Act ss. 92-93 to contributed property.
open_questions: Sources conflict on family provision: one guide says dependants may claim under the 1975-style Act, Ogier says Cayman courts cannot award dependants out of an estate. Succession Act 2021 Revision not read in full.
The firewall sections quoted from secondary summaries; primary text not read.
